subject: Post-call: load test scope and reproducibility checklist
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Joe Rodriguez <joe@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: load test scope and reproducibility checklist

Hi Joe — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a compact checklist so we can scope the benchmark run(s) and make them reproducible on our side. Please confirm the answers in bold or attach the prompt/data files when you can.

Summary of goals (from today's call)
- Target latency SLOs: p95 <= 250ms for user-facing text generation (8k context typical), p99 <= 500ms.
- Concurrency/throughput: sustained 20 RPS normal load, planned bursts up to 100 RPS for 30s during sales peaks.
- Streaming behavior: client expects incremental tokens every ~300ms for the streaming endpoint; full token stream must not pause for >600ms.
- Quality: your QA team will validate top-level correctness using the sample prompt set (see request below).

Items we need from BrightCart to set up an identical run environment:
1) Prompt set and representative dataset (CSV or JSONL) — include expected sequence lengths and any system messages.
2) Traffic profile: distribution over hour/day, burst timing, and auth token/traffic shaping to simulate.
3) Any blocking content filters or reranking steps that run post-generation.
4) Acceptance criteria for the test: pass/fail thresholds for latency, token-loss, and streaming stutter.

What we'll provide for a reproducible run:
- harness-config (example attached) with exact Docker image tag, git commit, and runner flags.
- measurement definitions: cold-start vs steady-state, warmup procedure (KV cache protocol), random seed handling, and log formats.
- raw sample logs and artifact links so you can reproduce runs locally if needed.

Next steps / asks (can we get these by EOD Thursday?):
- BrightCart to share prompt set and a short burst profile (CSV): preferred file format is CSV with a prompt_id, prompt_text, token_length_hint.
- Confirm whether 8k context is the dominant path or if 2k/32k paths are also important.
- Permission to run an initial 1-hour qualification run in your preferred region (we'll coordinate windows).

Thanks — I'll loop Marcus in for technical details and scheduling.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
A: +1 415-555-0183

From: Joe Rodriguez <joe@brightcart.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: load test scope and reproducibility checklist

Thanks Aisha — great summary. Confirming details and attaching an initial prompt set.

Answers inline: 
- Latency SLO: our primary ask is p95 <= 250ms on the 8k context path (this is what our product considers interactive). p99 <= 500ms is desirable but not blocking for go/no-go.
- Traffic profile: normal steady-state ~20 RPS for storefront recommendations. We run rare marketing spikes up to 100 RPS for ~30s; these are the ones we want to validate graceful degradation on.
- Streaming: yes — we expect partial tokens delivered in <300ms increments for the interactive path. If streaming degrades we will surface to UX.

Attachments: prompt_set_brightcart_v1.csv (attached), short-burst-profile.csv (included inline).

Quick questions for reproducibility: 
1) How do you define "warm" vs "cold" for KV cache sequences? Do you use a fixed warmup token count or dataset flush?
2) Will you include the exact Docker image and commit hash in the harness artifact (we need this to reproduce)?
3) Can you share the log schema so our SREs can parse and compare?

We can provide a synthetic user-id distribution and a sample of production logs if that helps.

Joe Rodriguez
Director, Infrastructure
BrightCart
joe@brightcart.com

Attachments: prompt_set_brightcart_v1.csv

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Joe Rodriguez <joe@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: load test scope and reproducibility checklist

Forwarding Joe's response + prompt set. Marcus / Monica — can you review and draft an initial reproducibility plan? High-level asks below; please keep it lean and runnable.

Immediate scope for the perf team:
- Define measurement definitions (strings we will publish): p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput (tokens/sec), streaming inter-token gap distribution, token-loss, and error-rate. Explicitly separate cold-start (first request after container boot) vs warm steady-state.
- Warmup protocol: recommend a deterministic warmup sequence (we should replay 5 unique prompt_ids x 10 each) and a 2-minute KV cache prefill by replaying a customer-provided dataset.
- Determinism: include exact Docker image tag, Git commit SHA, harness runner version, and seed for any randomized sampling. Add a manifest file to artifacts.
- Harness config: attach example (harness-config-example.yaml) and highlight fields to pin (image, commit, concurrency, batch size, tokenization).
- Logging and artifact outputs: produce compressed raw logs plus a parsed CSV of per-request metrics and a reconciliation script.

Can you draft a short doc (one pager) that we can share with Joe that lists the above plus a proposed run window (we should propose Wed 2026-12-02 09:00-11:00 PT for an initial qualification run).

Thanks — cc'ing Joe so BrightCart sees the plan.

—Aisha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-11-30T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: load test scope and reproducibility checklist

Thanks Aisha — sketching the plan and timeline below. I'll own the harness changes; Monica will coordinate scheduling and QA validation.

Planned deliverables (by EOD Monday 2026-11-30):
- One-pager to BrightCart with measurement definitions and the proposed run plan (will attach).
- Harness repo PR that pins image tag + commit + runner version and adds a manifest artifact. Link: https://github.com/redwoodinference/perf-harness/pull/642 (working branch brightcart/replicable-runs).
- Configs: harness-config-example.yaml (attached) with fields to pin: image: redwood/serve:20261124-rc1, commit: a1b2c3d4, concurrency: 50, target_rps: 20, burst_rps: 100, max_seq_len: 8192.
- Warmup: deterministic replay of prompt_ids [101..110] twice, then a 2-minute KV prefill pass. We'll record the first 10 requests as cold-start and exclude them from steady-state metrics.
- Logging: JSONL raw logs + per-request CSV (request_id,timestamp,latency_ms,bytes_out,tokens_out,stream_gaps_ms,error_code). We'll share parsing script and sample logs (run-sample-logs.txt).

Proposed initial run window: Wed 2026-12-02 09:00-11:00 PT. If BrightCart prefers evening or a different region, we'll mirror.

Open questions for BrightCart:
- Do you want us to also run the 2k and 32k context paths, or focus solely on 8k?
- Confirm whether streaming cadence of <=300ms is measured at the client-facing token emission or at our server's flush intervals (we recommend measuring at the client).

I'll create the one-pager and post the link here when ready.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
